summary: Underneath is a real viscous-shell glassblowing simulation, but neither post looks like glassblowing. A yellow, opaque, plastic-looking egg swells on a pipe that nobody holds, and as it cools it breaks into a mosaic of jagged red triangles. The night still is a red blob in heavy noise, with no context to place it.
real_change: physics/glassblow.jl is a real simulation. It treats the gather as a thin Newtonian membrane on an icosphere, with Trouton membrane stress and a viscous bending dashpot on the hinges. Each step solves an implicit sparse-Cholesky system with breath pressure, gravity in the turning, dipping pipe frame, and inertia. Each triangle keeps its volume, so thickness is volume/area. Each triangle cools by radiation and convection according to its own thickness, viscosity follows a VFT fit to soda-lime, and a triangle tears below 0.15 mm. sphere_test checks the shell against the closed form dR/dt = pR^2/(12 eta h). Some things are only drawn or scripted: the colour, which is Planck emission per vertex from the solved temperatures; the pipe; and the 'breath', a scripted plan(t) of 600 Pa for 5 s, half a turn per second for 3 s, then a 57 degree dip. Nobody blows. It is an offline movie script (movies/glassblow.jl), not something you can do in the game. The plugin the session changed, tops.jl (a tippe top you spin with key 1), appears in neither post.
surprise_why: A temperature-dependent viscous glass membrane that inflates, sags and stiffens is new physics the island never had. It is a nice step past the kiln and glaze posts, but on screen it reads as a yellow balloon turning red.
fun_why: There is nothing to do. Lumi never touches it, the breath is a scripted curve, and the clip is one blob growing and changing colour for 8 seconds, so you watch it once.
real_why: It is an engineered implicit FE viscous shell with real material constants, thickness-driven cooling, a VFT viscosity and a closed-form check. It is let down by running only offline, by the scripted breath, and by the coarse per-triangle temperature showing through as facets.

findings.what: Nobody blows or holds the pipe. The caption says the gather 'takes my breath', but no body is anywhere near. A bare pipe enters from the frame edge, its far end unheld. It swings from level to steeply dipped on its own, and the bubble inflates with no one at the other end.
findings.where: blowing-glass, every storyboard frame; the pipe swings at 3.0-3.5 s (frames 7-8); hot-glass-lights-the-sand
findings.evidence: The pipe runs off the left edge in frames 1-6 and off the top edge in frames 7-16, and no character is visible. In movies/glassblow.jl:10, gb_plan(t) supplies the pressure and pitch as a function of time.
findings.suggestion: Put Lumi at the end of the pipe, with the cheeks or body pulsing in time with the pressure curve and the hands turning and dipping the pipe. Better still, let the player hold a key to blow, as tops.jl does for the wind.

findings.what: As the glass cools it shatters visually into a mosaic of jagged red triangles and sawtooth bands. These are mesh facets, not a smooth gradient. The glass also reads as opaque yellow plastic (a lemon or balloon), not glass: no transparency, refraction or glossy highlight.
findings.where: blowing-glass at 75% and storyboard frames 13-16; also the white flat blotches on the bubble in hot-glass-glow.png
findings.evidence: Hard-edged red triangles cover the top of the egg at 75% and spread to most of it by the end. The bubble is a flat saturated yellow in daylight. In the night still it has white, cut-out-looking patches.
findings.suggestion: Subdivide or smooth the per-triangle temperature before mapping it to colour, and render the glass with a dielectric material plus emission so that cooler parts turn clear rather than red plastic.

findings.what: 'Its thinnest walls go dark and stiff first' is not visible. Nothing in the film goes dark or stiff: the whole bubble shifts from yellow to orange-red, and the red patches sit near the pipe. The night still is mostly noise, and a red blob on a black stick over grain gives no sense of sand or of the island.
findings.where: blowing-glass caption against storyboard frames 12-16; hot-glass-lights-the-sand
findings.evidence: The last frames show a uniform red egg with darker triangle fringes at the top. There is no frame where some regions are clearly frozen while others keep moving. In hot-glass-glow.png the ground is uniform speckle with no sand texture or surroundings.
findings.suggestion: Show thickness or viscosity side by side (a cut-away, or a slow pan), and let the glow dim visibly where the wall has thinned. Render the night still with more samples and include something recognisable on the ground.
